statement: For an infinite-horizon dynamic decision problem with state $x$, available action set $\Gamma(x)$, deterministic state transition function $T(x, a)$, instantaneous payoff $F(x, a)$, and discount factor $0 < \beta < 1$, the optimal value function $V(x)$ satisfies the functional equation: $$V(x) = \max_{a \in \Gamma(x)} \{ F(x, a) + \beta V(T(x, a)) \}$$

symbols.meaning: state variable at time t (with x_0 denoting the initial state, or x when time subscripts are omitted)
action representing values for one or more control variables taken at time t (or a when time subscripts are omitted)
set of actions available to be taken at state x
transition function determining the new state when action a is taken in state x
current payoff from taking action a in state x
value function describing the optimal obtainable value of the objective function starting from state x
policy function describing the optimal action as a function of the state

steps.text:
Define the infinite-horizon decision problem for an initial state $x_0$, specifying the value function $V(x_0)$ as the maximum sum of discounted payoffs over all feasible action sequences:
$$V(x_0) = \max_{\{a_t\}_{t=0}^{\infty}} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \beta^t F(x_t, a_t)$$
subject to the constraints $a_t \in \Gamma(x_t)$ and $x_{t+1} = T(x_t, a_t)$ for all $t = 0, 1, 2, \dots$

Apply Bellman's principle of optimality to isolate the initial choice $a_0$ at time 0 from the subsequent choices starting from time 1 at state $x_1 = T(x_0, a_0)$:
$$V(x_0) = \max_{a_0} \left\{ F(x_0, a_0) + \beta \left[ \max_{\{a_t\}_{t=1}^\infty} \sum_{t=1}^\infty \beta^{t-1} F(x_t, a_t) : a_t \in \Gamma(x_t), x_{t+1} = T(x_t, a_t), \forall t \geq 1 \right] \right\}$$
subject to $a_0 \in \Gamma(x_0)$ and $x_1 = T(x_0, a_0)$.

Identify the bracketed expression as the value of the decision problem beginning at time 1 from state $x_1 = T(x_0, a_0)$, which by definition is $V(x_1)$, yielding the recursive definition:
$$V(x_0) = \max_{a_0} \{ F(x_0, a_0) + \beta V(x_1) \}$$
subject to $a_0 \in \Gamma(x_0)$ and $x_1 = T(x_0, a_0)$.

Drop the time subscripts and substitute the transition law $x_1 = T(x, a)$ directly into the value function argument to obtain the stationary Bellman functional equation:
$$V(x) = \max_{a \in \Gamma(x)} \{ F(x, a) + \beta V(T(x, a)) \}$$

assumptions.assumption: Algebraic structure has a total ordering
assumptions.breaks_when: The structure has only a partial ordering, requiring the generic Bellman's equation

assumptions.assumption: The decision problem satisfies the principle of optimality (optimal substructure)
assumptions.breaks_when: An optimal policy does not have the property that remaining decisions constitute an optimal policy with regard to the state resulting from the first decision

assumptions.assumption: State transitions and immediate payoffs are stationary functions of current state and action alone
assumptions.breaks_when: Payoffs or transitions depend on the past history of states and actions

failure_modes.signature: Numerical backwards induction becomes computationally infeasible
failure_modes.cause: Vast number of possible actions and potential state variables that must be considered

failure_modes.signature: Standard Bellman maximization cannot totally order payoffs
failure_modes.cause: Underlying algebraic structure possesses only a partial ordering rather than a total ordering

failure_modes.signature: Model misspecification or inability to compute the policy function
failure_modes.cause: Difficulties in choosing or observing the discount rate \beta
